import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Conjecture 7.56

by N. S. Chernikov

Does a group satisfy the minimum (respectively, maximum) condition on subgroups if it is a product
of two subgroups satisfying the minimum (respectively, maximum) condition on subgroups?

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/

namespace Kourovka.«7.56»

/--
Does a group $G$ satisfy the minimum condition on subgroups if $G$ is the set product $AB$ of two
subgroups $A$ and $B$ that each satisfy the minimum condition on subgroups? Here $G = AB$ means
that every $g \in G$ can be written as $g = ab$ with $a \in A$ and $b \in B$.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem kourovka.«7.56».parts.i : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∀ (G : Type*) [Group G] (A B : Subgroup G),
      (∀ g : G, ∃ a ∈ A, ∃ b ∈ B, g = a * b) →
      WellFoundedLT (Subgroup A) → WellFoundedLT (Subgroup B) →
      WellFoundedLT (Subgroup G) := by
  sorry

/--
Does a group $G$ satisfy the maximum condition on subgroups if $G$ is the set product $AB$ of two
subgroups $A$ and $B$ that each satisfy the maximum condition on subgroups? Here $G = AB$ means
that every $g \in G$ can be written as $g = ab$ with $a \in A$ and $b \in B$.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem kourovka.«7.56».parts.ii : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∀ (G : Type*) [Group G] (A B : Subgroup G),
      (∀ g : G, ∃ a ∈ A, ∃ b ∈ B, g = a * b) →
      WellFoundedGT (Subgroup A) → WellFoundedGT (Subgroup B) →
      WellFoundedGT (Subgroup G) := by
  sorry

end Kourovka.«7.56»
modeling_decisions: Interpreted the minimum condition on subgroups of a group X as `WellFoundedLT (Subgroup X)`, and the maximum condition as `WellFoundedGT (Subgroup X)`, following the fixed decomposition and Mathlib's strict inclusion order.
Expressed `G = AB` elementwise as `∀ g : G, ∃ a ∈ A, ∃ b ∈ B, g = a * b`; this preserves the ordered set product and does not assume normality or replace it with the subgroup join.
Treated the minimum and maximum readings of “respectively” as two co-equal yes/no questions, each with its own `answer(sorry)`.
Used `Subgroup A` and `Subgroup B` for the subgroup lattices of the abstract groups carried by the subgroup subtypes.

by N. S. Chernikov

(B. Amberg). Does a group satisfy the minimum (respectively, maximum) condition
on subgroups if it is a product of two subgroups satisfying the minimum
(respectively, maximum) condition on subgroups?

A group $G$ is a *product* of its subgroups $A$ and $B$ if $G = AB$ as sets, that is,
every $g \in G$ can be written as $g = ab$ with $a \in A$, $b \in B$. The subgroups $A$
and $B$ need not be normal, so $G = AB$ is stated as the pointwise product of sets
`(A : Set G) * (B : Set G) = Set.univ`, not as the join `A ⊔ B = ⊤`.

chain of its subgroups is finite, i.e. `WellFoundedLT (Subgroup G)`. It satisfies
the *maximum condition on subgroups* if every strictly ascending chain of its
subgroups is finite, i.e. `WellFoundedGT (Subgroup G)` (equivalently, every subgroup
is finitely generated).

The two readings of "respectively" are independent questions, stated as parts (i)
and (ii).

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)

namespace Kourovka.«7.56»

/--
Does a group satisfy the minimum condition on subgroups if it is a product of two
subgroups satisfying the minimum condition on subgroups?

Here $G = AB$ means every element of $G$ is a product $ab$ with $a \in A$ and $b \in B$,
and the minimum condition on subgroups of a group $H$ is `WellFoundedLT (Subgroup H)`:
every strictly descending chain of subgroups of $H$ is finite.
-/

theorem kourovka.«7.56».parts.i : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∀ (G : Type) [Group G] (A B : Subgroup G),
      (A : Set G) * (B : Set G) = Set.univ →
      WellFoundedLT (Subgroup A) → WellFoundedLT (Subgroup B) →
      WellFoundedLT (Subgroup G) := by
  sorry

/--
Does a group satisfy the maximum condition on subgroups if it is a product of two
subgroups satisfying the maximum condition on subgroups?

Here $G = AB$ means every element of $G$ is a product $ab$ with $a \in A$ and $b \in B$,
and the maximum condition on subgroups of a group $H$ is `WellFoundedGT (Subgroup H)`:
every strictly ascending chain of subgroups of $H$ is finite.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem kourovka.«7.56».parts.ii : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∀ (G : Type) [Group G] (A B : Subgroup G),
      (A : Set G) * (B : Set G) = Set.univ →
      WellFoundedGT (Subgroup A) → WellFoundedGT (Subgroup B) →
      WellFoundedGT (Subgroup G) := by
  sorry

end Kourovka.«7.56»

by N. S. Chernikov

(B. Amberg). Does a group satisfy the minimum (respectively, maximum) condition on
subgroups if it is a product of two subgroups satisfying the minimum (respectively,
maximum) condition on subgroups?

A group $G$ is the *product* of two subgroups $A$ and $B$ if
$G = AB = \{ab : a \in A,\ b \in B\}$. The subgroups $A$ and $B$ are not assumed to be
normal, so this is stated with the pointwise set product `(A : Set G) * B = Set.univ`
and not with the join `A ⊔ B`.

A group satisfies the *minimum condition on subgroups* if every strictly descending chain
of subgroups is finite, i.e. `<` on `Subgroup G` is well-founded (`WellFoundedLT`).
It satisfies the *maximum condition on subgroups* if every strictly ascending chain of
subgroups is finite, i.e. `>` on `Subgroup G` is well-founded (`WellFoundedGT`).

The two readings of "respectively" are independent questions and are stated separately.

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/

open scoped Pointwise

namespace Kourovka.«7.56»

/--
Does a group satisfy the minimum condition on subgroups if it is a product of two
subgroups satisfying the minimum condition on subgroups?

That is: let $G$ be a group with subgroups $A$ and $B$ such that $G = AB$. If $A$ and $B$
satisfy the minimum condition on subgroups, must $G$ satisfy the minimum condition on
subgroups?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem kourovka.«7.56».parts.i : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∀ (G : Type) [Group G] (A B : Subgroup G),
      (A : Set G) * (B : Set G) = Set.univ →
      WellFoundedLT (Subgroup A) → WellFoundedLT (Subgroup B) →
      WellFoundedLT (Subgroup G) := by
  sorry

/--
Does a group satisfy the maximum condition on subgroups if it is a product of two
subgroups satisfying the maximum condition on subgroups?

That is: let $G$ be a group with subgroups $A$ and $B$ such that $G = AB$. If $A$ and $B$
satisfy the maximum condition on subgroups, must $G$ satisfy the maximum condition on
subgroups?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem kourovka.«7.56».parts.ii : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∀ (G : Type) [Group G] (A B : Subgroup G),
      (A : Set G) * (B : Set G) = Set.univ →
      WellFoundedGT (Subgroup A) → WellFoundedGT (Subgroup B) →
      WellFoundedGT (Subgroup G) := by
  sorry

end Kourovka.«7.56»
